figures.finding: Rwanda has no standing film fund yet: the Rwanda Film Office (set up in 2019 in the Rwanda Development Board) says it is working to establish one; its 2024 Creative Grants Initiative, co-financed equally with the Francophonie, gave EUR 360,000 to four projects (two in production, two in post-production).

grants2024.cofinanced: RDB and OIF equally, with the ACP-EU Culture Programme

sources.said: This year, four promising film projects — two in production and two in post-production — have been awarded a total of €360,000 in funding. The grants are co-financed equally by the Rwanda Development Board and the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie

The Rwanda Film Office (RFO), established in 2019 under the Rwanda Development Board (RDB), serves as a central hub for audiovisual and film industry services. … The RFO is also focused on establishing a Film Fund to drive the development of local film projects and attract international productions to Rwanda.

figures.finding: The Film Office's first pilot call (September 2022) had RWF 184 million for up to 26 projects, with grants from RWF 200,000 for pitch support up to RWF 30 million for production and RWF 82.5 million for an international co-production co-funded by the Francophonie.

sources.said: The Rwanda Film Office initiated a call for projects with a total budget of 184 million RWF to support filmmakers at various stages of production, from writing to post-production. … The grants start from 200.000 RWF for “pitch support” up to 30.000.000 RWF for production and 82.500.000 RWF for an international co-production
